properties.description: Discounted price should be non-negative for valid inputs
properties.evidence: @param discount - Discount percentage (0-100); prices should not go negative

properties.description: Discount should not increase the price when discount is positive
properties.evidence: Discount reduces price; @param discount - Discount percentage (0-100)

properties.description: Zero discount returns original price unchanged
properties.evidence: Zero discount means no change to price

properties.description: 100% discount results in zero price
properties.evidence: 100% discount = free; price * (1 - 100/100) = 0

properties.description: Total of empty array is zero
properties.evidence: @param prices - Array of item prices; empty cart costs nothing

properties.description: Total of single-item array equals the item
properties.evidence: Single item total = the item itself

properties.description: Total is non-negative when all prices are non-negative
properties.evidence: @returns Total sum; sum of non-negative numbers is non-negative

properties.description: Output always has exactly 2 decimal places
properties.evidence: @returns Formatted string like "99.99"; toFixed(2) always gives 2 decimals

properties.description: Parsing formatted price back gives approximately the original
properties.evidence: Formatted price should round-trip within rounding tolerance

properties.description: Zero discount returns the original price unchanged
properties.evidence: applyDiscount returns price * (1 - discount / 100). When discount=0, this is price * 1 = price.

properties.description: 100% discount returns zero
properties.evidence: applyDiscount returns price * (1 - 100/100) = price * 0 = 0.

properties.description: Discounted price is between 0 and original price (inclusive) for valid inputs
properties.evidence: For price >= 0 and 0 <= discount <= 100, the factor (1 - discount/100) is in [0, 1], so result is in [0, price].

properties.description: Higher discount yields lower or equal price (monotonically decreasing in discount)
properties.assertion: discount1 <= discount2 implies applyDiscount(price, discount1) >= applyDiscount(price, discount2)
properties.evidence: applyDiscount = price * (1 - discount/100). Since price >= 0, increasing discount decreases the result.

properties.description: Discount is linear: applying discount d to price p equals p - p*d/100
properties.evidence: price * (1 - discount/100) is algebraically equivalent to price - price * discount / 100.

properties.description: Total of an empty array is zero
properties.evidence: reduce with initial value 0 on an empty array returns 0.

properties.description: Total of a single-element array equals that element
properties.evidence: reduce over a single element with initial 0 returns 0 + element = element.

properties.description: Concatenating two arrays gives a total equal to the sum of their individual totals (conservation/additivity)
properties.evidence: Sum is additive: sum(a ++ b) = sum(a) + sum(b). The reduce-based implementation preserves this.

properties.description: Order of items does not affect the total (commutativity of addition)
properties.evidence: Addition is commutative, so reversing the array should not change the sum.

properties.description: Total of non-negative prices is non-negative
properties.evidence: Sum of non-negative numbers is non-negative. Doc says prices are item prices (non-negative).

properties.description: Output always contains exactly one decimal point
properties.evidence: toFixed(2) always produces a string with exactly 2 decimal places, which includes exactly one '.' character.

properties.description: Output always has exactly 2 digits after the decimal point
properties.evidence: toFixed(2) guarantees exactly 2 decimal digits in the output string.

properties.description: Parsing the formatted string back yields a value within 0.005 of the original (roundtrip within rounding tolerance)
properties.evidence: toFixed(2) rounds to 2 decimal places, so parseFloat(formatPrice(x)) is within 0.005 of x.

properties.description: Formatting is idempotent: formatting the parsed result of a formatted price gives the same string
properties.evidence: After toFixed(2) and parseFloat, the value already has at most 2 decimal places, so a second toFixed(2) produces the same string.

properties.description: Output string is a valid number (can be parsed back to a finite number)
properties.evidence: toFixed(2) on a finite number produces a valid numeric string that parseFloat can parse back to a finite number.

properties.description: Output length equals input length
properties.evidence: Sorting should not add or remove elements

properties.description: Output is monotonically non-decreasing
properties.assertion: sortNumbers(arr).every((v, i, a) => i === 0 || a[i-1] <= v)
properties.evidence: @returns New sorted array; ascending order

properties.description: Sorting is idempotent
properties.evidence: Sorting an already sorted array should be a no-op

properties.description: Output has no duplicate elements
properties.evidence: Uses new Set() which removes duplicates

properties.description: Output length is at most input length
properties.evidence: Removing duplicates can only reduce or maintain length

properties.description: Unique is idempotent
properties.evidence: Applying unique to already-unique array should be a no-op

properties.description: Output length equals sum of input lengths
properties.evidence: Merge should include all elements from both arrays

properties.description: Reversing twice returns original
properties.evidence: Reverse is its own inverse: reverse(reverse(x)) === x

properties.description: Length is preserved after reversing
properties.evidence: Reversing characters does not change count

properties.description: First character becomes last character
properties.evidence: Reversing puts first element at the end

properties.description: Output length never exceeds maxLen
properties.evidence: @param maxLen - Maximum length; result should respect this limit

properties.description: Short strings are returned unchanged
properties.assertion: str.length <= maxLen ? truncate(str, maxLen) === str : true
properties.evidence: if (str.length <= maxLen) return str — code returns unchanged

properties.description: Truncated strings end with ellipsis
properties.evidence: return str.slice(0, maxLen - 3) + '...' — adds ellipsis

properties.description: Empty string is a palindrome
properties.evidence: Empty string reversed equals itself

properties.description: Single characters are palindromes
properties.evidence: Any single character reads the same forwards and backwards

properties.description: Concatenating a string with its reverse is always a palindrome
properties.evidence: str + reverse(str) is always a palindrome by construction

properties.description: Addition is commutative
properties.evidence: Addition: a + b == b + a for all integers

properties.description: Zero is identity element for addition
properties.evidence: a + 0 = a; additive identity

properties.description: Addition is associative
properties.assertion: add(add(a, b), c) === add(a, add(b, c))
properties.evidence: (a + b) + c == a + (b + c); associativity of addition

properties.description: Division by 1 returns the original number
properties.evidence: a / 1 = a; division by unity identity

properties.description: Division of zero always returns zero
properties.evidence: 0 / b = 0 for any non-zero b
